channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Paraná Pesquisas: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 48,1% e Lula soma 40,3% no 2º turno em SP
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro leads with 48.1% of voting intentions against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who has 40.3%, in a potential runoff scenario for the 2026 elections in São Paulo, according to Paraná Pesquisas.

item.title: 'Diálogo vai resolver sucessão no Rio', diz Douglas Ruas, eleito presidente da Alerj
item.description: Douglas Ruas, president of the Alerj and backed by Flávio Bolsonaro, states that dialogue will resolve the Rio de Janeiro succession, avoiding judicial battles. He seeks to accelerate his governorship via an STF petition, emphasizing the constitutional line of succession after Cláudio Castro's conviction and dual vacancy in the governorship.

item.title: Sem citar Trump, Brasil, México e Espanha cobram respeito à soberania de Cuba e dizem que vão 'intensificar' ajuda ao país
item.description: Brazil, Mexico, and Spain issued a joint statement demanding respect for Cuba's sovereignty and announcing intensified humanitarian aid amid the island's energy and food crisis. The statement, while not directly naming Donald Trump, emphasizes the need for respectful dialogue in line with international law, following Trump's remarks that Cuba would be 'next' after U.S. actions in Venezuela and Iran.

item.title: A solução para Dias Toffoli na crise do STF
item.description: STF ministers, speaking anonymously, advocate for reforms to address the Court's image crisis, including proposals such as granting Dias Toffoli a leave of absence amid controversies tied to the Banco Master case and his connection to a resort linked to investigated funds. President Lula has reportedly expressed a long-standing desire to remove Toffoli from the Court, rooted in personal grievance over Toffoli blocking Lula from attending his brother's funeral during the Lava-Jato era. While some suggest Toffoli step down, others warn that impeaching ministers could set a dangerous precedent for future institutional instability.

item.title: Lula elogia Espanha por barrar aviões dos EUA para o Irã
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva praised Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez for blocking U.S. warplanes from using Spanish airspace to attack Iran, speaking at the first Global Progressive Mobilization meeting in Barcelona. Lula condemned recent U.S.-led military interventions in Iraq, Libya, and Gaza, arguing they follow a pattern of using false pretenses to bomb civilians, and accused the five permanent UN Security Council members of acting as 'warlords'. He claimed the world is experiencing more armed conflicts than since World War II.

item.title: Saiba quem estava com Lula na cúpula progressista na Espanha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attended the 4th High-Level Meeting of the Forum for the Defense of Democracy in Barcelona, Spain, posing alongside the presidents of Cape Verde, José Maria Neves, and Uruguay, Yamandú Orsi. During the event, Lula urged the permanent UN Security Council members (Trump, Macron, Putin, Xi Jinping and Starmer) to end war and criticized neoliberalism for delivering hunger, inequality and insecurity. His European trip included over 30 expected agreements with Spain and Germany, accompanied by a delegation of at least 14 ministers and state company presidents.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 48,1% e Lula soma 40,3% no segundo turno em São Paulo, diz Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads with 48.1% against Lula's 40.3% in a hypothetical second-round scenario in São Paulo, according to Paraná Pesquisas conducted from April 10–14. In the first round, the two are technically tied, with Bolsonaro slightly ahead at 39.3% versus Lula's 36%. The margin of error is 2.5 percentage points.

item.title: Na Espanha, Lula fala em “desmascarar” oposição
item.description: President Lula urged in Barcelona the need to 'unmask' the opposition, accusing them of claiming to stand with the people while governing for the rich, and stated that the far right had planned a coup in Brazil. He also criticized left-wing governments that adopt austerity after winning on progressive platforms, betraying public trust. Lula spoke at the 1st Global Progressive Mobilization meeting in Spain, alongside leaders such as Sheinbaum, Petro, Orsi, and Ramaphosa.

item.title: Lula diz que ‘esquerda se tornou o sistema’ e que precisa ‘praticar a coerência’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that the left has become part of the system by adopting neoliberal and austerity policies, allowing the right to position itself as anti-system. He urged left-wing parties to practice coherence by implementing their elected platforms and blamed billionaires, not minorities like LGBT+ individuals or immigrants, for social frustrations.

item.title: La izquierda internacional consagra a Sánchez: “Ha hecho algo extraordinario”
item.description: International progressive leaders, including Lula, Elly Schlein, Claudia Sheinbaum, and Zohran Mamdani, praised Pedro Sánchez for his leadership in revitalizing the global progressive movement. They highlighted his extraordinary achievements during a period of ideological weakness, viewing him as a symbol of resistance and hope against rising conservative forces like those of Donald Trump. The unanimous support reflects confidence that progressivism can regain ground internationally.

item.title: Alckmin diz que 26 estados aceitam a proposta de subvenção ao diesel importado
item.description: Acting President Geraldo Alckmin announced that 26 states have accepted the federal proposal to subsidize imported diesel, offering R$1.20 per liter split equally between the federal government and states, aiming to mitigate the impact of the Middle East war on fuel prices, inflation, and supply. The measure is voluntary, unlike the 2022 mandatory policy under Bolsonaro that led to R$25 billion in state compensation. The estimated fiscal impact is R$1.5 billion per month.

item.title: Lula critica Conselho de Segurança da ONU e pede mudanças
item.description: President Lula criticized the UN Security Council's inaction on global conflicts, demanding behavioral change from its five permanent members (U.S., China, Russia, France, UK). He condemned passivity in wars such as those in Iran, Ukraine, and Gaza, rejected unilateral threats by leaders like Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, and advocated for multilateralism and extraordinary UN meetings.

item.title: O mistério sobre a (não) desistência de Ciro Nogueira do projeto vice-presidencial
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, president of the Progressistas party, is negotiating with Flávio Bolsonaro for the support of the União Progressista federation in Bolsonaro’s presidential ticket, despite publicly stating his chances of being vice-president are zero and favoring names like Tereza Cristina. In private conversations, however, he confessed he still dreams of the vice-presidential slot, citing his ability to penetrate the PT’s Northeastern base and claiming Jair Bolsonaro had selected him for the role in October 2025, before Flávio announced his own candidacy.

item.title: Lula critica ataques ao Irã: 'Parem com essa loucura de guerra'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the attacks on Iran, denying that the country seeks to build a nuclear bomb and accusing the U.S. and Israel of inventing lies to justify war. He directly addressed the five permanent members of the UN Security Council — Trump, Xi Jinping, Putin, Macron, and Starmer — urging them to fulfill their duty to maintain global peace and end 'this madness of war'.

item.title: 56% apoiam e 35% discordam de prisão domiciliar para Bolsonaro, diz Ipsos
item.description: 56% of Brazilians support Jair Bolsonaro's 90-day house arrest for health reasons, while 35% oppose it. Among his 2022 voters, 69% support the measure; among Lula voters, 49% support and 42% oppose. After the initial period, 49% favor continuing house arrest if health permits, and 42% want a return to closed regime.

item.title: Lula volta a criticar Conselho de Segurança da ONU; "cinco membros permanentes se transformaram em cinco senhores de guerra"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva again criticized the UN Security Council, accusing its five permanent members of becoming 'lords of war' instead of preserving peace. He named each member individually and urged them to fulfill their obligations and end the 'madness'.

item.title: Senadores da oposição entram com recurso para anular derrota de relatório na CPI do Crime
item.description: Opposition senators Eduardo Girão, Magno Malta, and Marcos do Val filed a request to annul the vote on the Organized Crime CPI report, which was defeated six to four, arguing that strategic substitutions by government allies artificially altered the committee's balance during the final session. The report by Senator Alessandro Vieira had called for the indictment of STF ministers and the PGR over allegations of bias and interference in investigations, but was rejected after Moro and do Val left and were replaced by PT senators aligned with the government.

item.title: "Ninguém precisar ter medo no mundo democrático de ser o que é", diz Lula em fórum na Espanha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated in Barcelona that no one should fear being who they are or speaking their mind in a democratic world, as long as democratic rules established by society are respected. The remarks were made during the 1st Global Progressive Mobilization Meeting in Spain.

item.title: Alckmin, sobre candidatura de Caiado: ‘Não desestimulo ninguém de ser candidato’
item.description: Acting President Geraldo Alckmin stated he does not discourage anyone from running for office, referencing former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado, and clarified his visit to Valparaíso de Goiás was technical, not political. He also emphasized progress on the regulatory framework for critical minerals in Brazil, noting that rapporteur Arnaldo Jardim is expected to present the report in the coming weeks.

item.title: Sheinbaum, Lula y Petro cierran filas en Barcelona para revertir el giro a la derecha de América Latina
item.description: Presidents of Brazil, Colombia, Uruguay and the Spanish Prime Minister met in Barcelona for the IV Meeting in Defense of Democracy, aiming to counter the rightward shift in Latin America. Lula da Silva, Gustavo Petro, Yamandú Orsi and Pedro Sánchez reinforced progressive regional cooperation. The meeting took place this Saturday as part of a coordinated effort to strengthen democratic institutions across the continent.

item.title: Boric advierte en España: “La democracia no es un estado natural de las cosas. Tenemos que cuidarla, es frágil”
item.description: Former Chilean president Gabriel Boric warned at the IV Summit in Defense of Democracy in Barcelona that democracy is not a natural state and must be nurtured daily, expressing concern over authoritarian projects exploiting citizen disengagement. He stressed the fragility of democratic institutions and the need for conscious effort to safeguard freedoms and human dignity, joining leaders such as Lula, Sánchez, and Sheinbaum.

item.title: Lula cobra mudança de comportamento de membros permanentes do Conselho de Segurança da ONU
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said the five permanent members of the UN Security Council must change their behavior after failing to stop the war in Iran. He made the remark during a leaders' summit in Barcelona, Spain, criticizing the body's ineffectiveness in addressing the conflict.

item.title: Zema recria cadeirada de Datena em Marçal
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) simulated a 'chair strike' against businessman and former coach Pablo Marçal during a Friday recording, in a joking tone. The gesture referenced the 2024 municipal elections incident where José Luiz Datena attacked Marçal with a chair during a televised debate. The post was published by O Antagonista.

item.title: Lula diz que nenhum país pode excluir integrantes do G20
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended the continued inclusion of all G20 members, criticizing unilateral exclusions, particularly referencing a potential removal of South Africa by the United States under Donald Trump. He stressed the importance of multilateralism, lamenting the lack of reform in institutions like the IMF and World Bank since the 2008 financial crisis, and called for greater representation of emerging economies and the Global South in international decision-making bodies such as the UN Security Council.

item.title: Pobres não podem pagar por irresponsabilidade das guerras, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva denounced ongoing wars, stating that the poor cannot bear the costs of the irresponsibility of conflicts, and advocated for strengthening multilateralism during his speech at the fourth high-level meeting of the Democracy Defense Forum in Barcelona.

item.title: Lula defende fim da 6x1 e diz que ganhos não podem valer só para ricos
item.description: President Lula advocated for ending the 6x1 work schedule, proposing a reduction of the workweek from 44 to 40 hours with two paid rest days, arguing that productivity gains should benefit poor workers as well. He stated that democracy loses credibility when it fails to respond to societal demands and emphasized the need for social progress to strengthen democracy. The proposal has broad popular support but faces resistance from business sectors.

item.title: STF receia ser alvo preferencial de candidatos
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) is facing an institutional crisis after the Organized Crime CPI report recommended the indictment of three ministers — Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes — raising concerns that the Court will become a central target in the 2026 electoral campaign. Ministers fear an anti-STF agenda will dominate the debate, with Gilmar Mendes filing a representation against the CPI rapporteur and internal dissatisfaction over the Court president’s perceived 'timid' response.

item.title: O Pacto Nacional contra o Feminicídio não pode ficar só no papel
item.description: The article denounces femicide in Brazil as a structural and widespread violence, noting that 1,568 women were killed in 2025 — nearly four per day — with figures likely underreported. While the National Pact against Femicide, launched in February 2026, represents progress by involving the three branches of government in measures such as accelerating protective orders and integrating data, the author warns it must not remain merely symbolic, given the deep historical and cultural roots of misogyny in the country.

item.title: Zema imita Datena e finge dar cadeirada em Marçal
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) simulated a chair strike on Pablo Marçal (União Brasil-SP) during a recording, referencing the 2024 electoral debate altercation between José Luiz Datena and Marçal in the São Paulo mayoral race. The stunt occurred ahead of a meeting between Zema and Marçal, who has backed right-wing candidates like Flávio Bolsonaro, aiming to defeat Lula in the 2026 presidential election.

item.title: Quase metade dos brasileiros defende a manutenção da prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro
item.description: Nearly half of Brazilians (49%) believe former President Jair Bolsonaro should remain under house arrest after the 90-day period ends, even if his health improves, while 42% think he should return to the 19th Military Police Battalion in Distrito Federal (Papudinha). A majority (56%) approve of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes’ decision to grant 90 days of house arrest for recovery from bilateral bacterial pneumonia. Support for maintaining house arrest is strongest among Bolsonaro voters (82%), those with household income above 5 minimum wages (60%), Southern residents (58%), evangelicals (58%), and respondents aged 60 or older (54%).

item.title: Alckmin diz que não é contra nem a favor da 'taxa das blusinhas' e afirma que apoiará decisão de Lula
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin stated he is neither for nor against the so-called 'blusinhas tax' and said he will fully support President Lula's decision on the measure, which applies to international purchases under US$50. He emphasized the decision must be made cautiously, considering industrial and employment impacts. The tax collected R$425 million in January 2025, a 25% increase compared to January 2024.

item.title: Precisamos regular tudo que é digital, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for expanding digital platform regulation in Brazil to ensure national sovereignty and prevent foreign interference, especially during the election year. He warned that without rules, big tech companies would establish 'digital colonialism,' extracting and monetizing data to concentrate political and economic power in the hands of a few billionaires. Lula stated that the Digital ECA (Felca Law) is only the first step in a broader regulatory process, without specifying future norms or implementation timelines.

item.title: 56% dos brasileiros concordam com prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro
item.description: An Ipsos-Ipec poll shows 56% of Brazilians agree with the 90-day house arrest granted to Jair Bolsonaro for health reasons, with 38% fully agreeing and 18% partially agreeing. Opinions are strongly tied to the 2022 presidential runoff vote: among those who fully agree, 54% voted for Bolsonaro and 30% for Lula. Agreement is higher in inland areas (58%) and cities with up to 50,000 inhabitants (60%) compared to state capitals (49%) and cities over 500,000 inhabitants (50%).

item.title: ‘Senhores da guerra’: As críticas de Lula à ONU em meio aos conflitos no Oriente Médio
item.description: President Lula criticized Donald Trump and the UN Security Council, accusing them of acting as 'lords of war' and undermining multilateralism. He called for extraordinary UN meetings to address global conflicts, citing impacts on the Brazilian economy, such as rising bean prices due to military escalation in the Middle East.

item.title: Relatório rejeitado abre novo embate entre Senado e Supremo
item.description: The rejection of the Organized Crime CPI report, which sought the indictment of STF ministers, intensified the conflict between the Senate and the Supreme Court, with analysts highlighting the political use of investigations amid the 2026 electoral calendar. The report was deemed legally weak and more electoral than investigative, benefiting senators like Alessandro Vieira and Davi Alcolumbre politically, though damaging their image of independence. The STF responded with filings at the PGR, deepening the tension between parliamentary immunity and judicial oversight of investigations.

item.title: Na Espanha, Lula pede reforma da ONU e controle global das plataformas digitais
item.description: President Lula advocated in Barcelona for the reform and expansion of the UN Security Council, criticizing the unilateral use of power by its permanent members and the lack of representation for countries like Brazil, Africa, Mexico, and India. He linked the weakening of multilateralism to the rise in global conflicts and indirectly criticized leaders such as Donald Trump for imposing decisions without international consensus.

item.title: Um antigo aliado pode aumentar a lista de problemas de Lula
item.description: Lula struggles to regain popularity, leading only in first-round polls while tied or trailing Flávio Bolsonaro in second-round scenarios. His campaign relies on popular measures like housing financing and fuel price controls, alongside efforts to strengthen state-level alliances, particularly in Ceará, where Governor Elmano de Freitas may lose to Ciro Gomes. A potential presidential bid by Ciro Gomes, encouraged by Aécio Neves’ PSD, poses a further threat as it could siphon left-wing votes and escalate criticism of Lula’s government, despite their past alliance.

item.title: Em Barcelona, Lula pede a Trump pelo fim no bloqueio econômico a Cuba
item.description: At the 4th High-Level Meeting of the Always Democracy Forum in Barcelona, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) made a direct appeal to Donald Trump to end the U.S. economic embargo against Cuba. He called the measure unjustified and harmful to the Cuban people, arguing that the humanitarian crisis on the island is worsened by isolation and that support — not blockade — should be the response. Lula also criticized U.S. foreign policy and urged the UN to play a stronger role in mediating global conflicts, including in the Middle East.

item.title: 'Selva urbana de crime e corrupção', diz Economist em análise sobre a crise de governança no Rio
item.description: The Economist highlights the stark contrast between Rio de Janeiro’s tourism boom and its deep governance crisis, defined by systemic corruption, territorial control by militias and criminal factions, and the removal or imprisonment of public officials. Despite 2.1 million international tourists in 2025 — a 45% increase — the state faces critical political instability, with former governor Cláudio Castro barred from office for eight years and ALERJ president Rodrigo Bacellar jailed over suspected drug trafficking ties. The Marielle Franco assassination and the Brazão brothers’ convictions reveal deep milician infiltration of institutions, while links between Flávio Bolsonaro and the family of slain militiaman Adriano da Nóbrega remain under scrutiny ahead of the 2026 presidential elections.

item.title: Lula critica líderes por guerra e cobra reação mais firme da ONU
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the UN's inaction and unilateral actions by major powers, citing invasions in Iraq, Libya, Ukraine, Iran, Gaza, and Venezuela as violations of multilateralism. He argued that unilateral decisions raise living costs in poor nations and advocated for reforming the multilateral system to prioritize hunger, illiteracy, and access to basic services. Lula also directly criticized the UN Security Council for its outdated structure and lack of representation.

item.title: “Extremismo continua vivo e vai disputar eleição outra vez”, diz Lula
item.description: Lula stated that political extremism in Brazil remains active despite the convictions related to the January 8 attacks, and that it will continue to contest elections. He referenced the imprisonment of Jair Bolsonaro during his speech at the 4th High-Level Meeting of the Forum in Defense of Democracy in Spain.

item.title: Ex-chefe do Conselhão assume agência de desenvolvimento industrial
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin appointed Olavo Noleto, former executive secretary of the Conselhão, as the new president of ABDI, Brazil’s Industrial Development Agency. Bruno Giovanni Reis was also named president of Embratur, replacing Marcelo Freixo, who is now a pre-candidate for federal deputy from Rio de Janeiro. Both appointments were published in an extra edition of the Official Gazette on Friday, April 17, 2026.

item.title: STF, Congresso e governo Lula: entenda o que está em jogo na ‘corrida desesperada’ das delações
item.description: The surge in plea bargains in Brazil has created institutional tension, with investigations into banks, investment funds, and criminal factions reaching the political class. Analysts describe a 'desperate race' for judicial cooperation, where early cooperators gain the greatest benefits, raising fears of a systemic scandal. At the same time, efforts in the STF and Congress to revise plea bargain rules and CPIs are viewed skeptically, as they appear driven by those under investigation.

item.title: Por que Minas Gerais virou um problema tanto para Lula quanto para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Minas Gerais has become a challenge for both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro due to the lack of solid electoral strongholds. Lula is banking on Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB), who has not yet confirmed his candidacy, while the PL is divided between supporting Governor Mateus Simões (PSD), Senator Cleitinho (Republicanos), or newcomer Flávio Roscoe — all of whom face electoral or ideological weaknesses.

item.title: Alessandro Vieira se posiciona entre Lula e Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) positioned himself in the 2026 presidential race by stating he stands between Lula and Bolsonaro, following his call for the indictment of three Supreme Court ministers and the Attorney General in the Organized Crime CPI. His statement comes amid extreme polarization, as Vieira seeks to present himself as a moderate alternative.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro supera Lula no 2º turno em SP, aponta pesquisa
item.description: A survey by Paraná Pesquisas released on January 18 shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leading President Lula (PT) with 48.1% voting intention in a hypothetical runoff in São Paulo, compared to Lula's 40.3%. Another 7.2% of respondents said they would vote for another candidate or were undecided. The poll indicates a 7.8-point advantage for Bolsonaro in the state.

item.title: Lula pede regulação global das redes sociais: 'Muito ódio, promiscuidade, sexo e jogatina'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva called for global regulation of social media during a left-wing leaders' forum in Barcelona, criticizing platforms for fostering hatred, promiscuity, sex, gambling, and disinformation. He argued that digital platforms are no longer 'social' and threaten national sovereignty, especially during election years, emphasizing that lies have prevailed over truth in public discourse.

item.title: Nos tornamos uma sociedade do medo?
item.description: Minister Toffoli of the STF claimed that criticizing ministers’ conduct amounts to attacking the institution and democracy, linking such acts to electoral crimes, as seen in the case of Senator Alessandro Vieira, who went from rapporteur to investigated. The text identifies a pattern of repression since 2019, beginning with the censorship of Crusoé magazine, extending to symbolic or minor acts like gestures, tweets, and airport remarks, fostering a climate of fear and self-censorship in Brazil.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: como está a disputa Lula x Flávio Bolsonaro após Datafolha e Quaest
item.description: Recent polls from Datafolha and Genial/Quaest show a tight race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical second-round scenario, with both candidates technically tied within the margin of error. Datafolha shows Bolsonaro at 46% and Lula at 45%, while Genial/Quaest records 42% for Bolsonaro and 40% for Lula. Both institutes note recent fluctuations and a highly polarized contest with no clear advantage for either candidate.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro derrotaria Lula no maior estado do país, diz Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leads President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a hypothetical presidential runoff in São Paulo state, with 48.1% to 40.3%, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey conducted April 11–14. The poll, based on 1,600 in-person interviews with a 2.5-point margin of error, shows Bolsonaro’s son defeating Lula in Brazil’s largest electoral college in a potential second-round matchup.
